correctness.rationale: Each cosine triple is the root set of 4X^3-3X-c. Differentiation in c converts the phase derivative of a symmetric sum into a strictly signed second divided difference of g′, whose sign equals that of g′′′. Apply this with positive third derivatives to exp(eu) and log(1-exp(-eu)), and a negative third derivative to exp(-eu). Exact Poisson algebra gives all four count probabilities and expected richness; mixtures over arbitrary nonnegative phase-independent shared effort retain strict comparison when positive effort occurs with positive probability. The closed-form phase gap and its unique positive effort maximizer follow by elementary hyperbolic algebra and the strictly decreasing sum of two coth functions. The embedded standard-library checker passed 34,603 finite numerical assertions on actual extracted package code. The proof, rather than finite checks, supports the infinite-parameter claim.

value.rationale: Real multi-taxon eDNA studies show different detection seasons, making the choice of what to optimize a practical mathematical ambiguity. This result gives a complete sharp contrast: maximizing expected richness or all-three detection selects the opposite season from maximizing at-least-two detection, even though any-positive chance is exactly season-invariant. The phase preference is robust to arbitrarily distributed shared detection quality, and its contrast has exactly one informative effort scale, distinguishing underpowered and saturated assays. These structural objective separations are more than a renamed Poisson formula or an arbitrary finite table. The illustrative parameters are not a field recommendation.
